\section{Class NP --- EXP}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.EXP
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\subsection*{Class NP --- EXP: Introduction}

This module introduces the exponential-time classes: $\mathrm{EXP}$ as the union of
the deterministic time classes $\mathrm{DTIME}(2^{n^c})$, and $\mathrm{NEXP}$ in
certificate form (exponential-length certificates checked by a polynomial-time
verifier language). It proves the chain of inclusions
$\mathrm{P} \subseteq \mathrm{EXP}$, $\mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{EXP}$ (by
brute-force certificate enumeration on a concrete multi-tape machine), and
$\mathrm{EXP} \subseteq \mathrm{NEXP}$ (by padding), together with the supporting
fixed-width binary counter, reversible logging/restoration, clean-call, and
exponential-split machinery.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\subsection*{Class NP --- EXP: Results}

\begin{definition}[The class $\mathrm{EXP}$]
\lean{Complexity.EXP}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p054-b004}
\label{Complexity.EXP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME}
A language $L$ over the binary alphabet belongs to $\mathrm{EXP}$ if and only if
$L \in \mathrm{DTIME}(2^{n^c})$ for some constant $c \in \mathbb{N}$, i.e.\ $L$ is
decided by some finite multi-tape Turing machine within $a \cdot 2^{n^c}$ steps on
inputs of length $n$, for constants $a$ and $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exponentially bounded function]
\lean{Complexity.ExpBound}
\label{Complexity.ExpBound}
\leanok
A function $p : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is \emph{exponentially bounded} if there
exist constants $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $p(n) \le C \cdot 2^{(n+1)^c}$ for
every $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The class $\mathrm{NEXP}$, certificate form]
\lean{Complexity.NEXP}
\label{Complexity.NEXP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P}
A language $L$ over the binary alphabet belongs to $\mathrm{NEXP}$ if there exist
constants $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$ and a verifier language $V \in \mathrm{P}$ such that
for every binary string $x$: $x \in L$ if and only if there is a certificate $u$ of
length exactly $C \cdot 2^{(|x|+1)^c}$ with the concatenation
$x \mathbin{+\!\!+} u$ in $V$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial time is contained in exponential time]
\lean{Complexity.P_subset_EXP}
\label{Complexity.P_subset_EXP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME.mono, Complexity.EXP, Complexity.P}
\difficulty{3}
Every language in $\mathsf{P}$ belongs to $\mathrm{EXP}$, the class of languages
decidable in time $2^{n^c}$ up to a constant factor for some natural number $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Little-endian value of a boolean word]
\lean{Complexity.enumValue}
\label{Complexity.enumValue}
\leanok
The value of a boolean word read as a little-endian binary numeral: the empty word
has value $0$, and a word with first bit $b$ and tail $u$ has value
$2 \cdot \mathrm{val}(u) + b$. Leading (high-order) zero bits are allowed.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fixed-width binary increment]
\lean{Complexity.enumInc}
\label{Complexity.enumInc}
\leanok
The fixed-width increment of a boolean word viewed as a little-endian binary
counter: it returns the incremented word of the same length, or nothing on
overflow (when the word is all ones); the empty word overflows.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Width-$w$ little-endian binary word]
\lean{Complexity.enumWord}
\label{Complexity.enumWord}
\leanok
For all natural numbers $w$ and $i$, the width-$w$ little-endian binary word of
$i$ is the list of the $w$ lowest binary digits of $i$, least significant first,
with high-order zeros retained.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Bound on a binary word value]
\lean{Complexity.enumValue_lt}
\label{Complexity.enumValue_lt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumValue}
\difficulty{2}
For every finite Boolean word $u$, its little-endian binary value is strictly less than
$2^{|u|}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Length of a fixed-width binary word]
\lean{Complexity.enumWord_length}
\label{Complexity.enumWord_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumWord}
\difficulty{2}
For all natural numbers $w$ and $i$, the width-$w$ little-endian binary word of $i$ has
length exactly $w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Zero represented at fixed width]
\lean{Complexity.enumWord_zero}
\label{Complexity.enumWord_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumWord}
\difficulty{2}
For every natural number $w$, the width-$w$ little-endian binary word of $0$ is the word
consisting of $w$ false bits.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Value of an in-range binary word]
\lean{Complexity.enumWord_value}
\label{Complexity.enumWord_value}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumValue, Complexity.enumWord}
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $w$ and $i$ with $i<2^w$, the little-endian value of the width-$w$
binary word of $i$ is $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Injectivity of binary word values]
\lean{Complexity.enumValue_injective}
\label{Complexity.enumValue_injective}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $u$ and $v$ be finite Boolean words of equal length. If their little-endian binary
values are equal, then $u=v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recovery of a word from its value]
\lean{Complexity.enumWord_complete}
\label{Complexity.enumWord_complete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumValue, Complexity.enumValue_injective, Complexity.enumValue_lt, Complexity.enumWord, Complexity.enumWord_length, Complexity.enumWord_value}
\difficulty{1}
For every finite Boolean word $u$, the width-$|u|$ little-endian binary word
representing its little-endian value is exactly $u$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Specification of fixed-width increment]
\lean{Complexity.enumInc_spec}
\label{Complexity.enumInc_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumInc, Complexity.enumValue}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean word $u$, if its fixed-width increment is a word $v$, then $v$ has the
same length as $u$ and its little-endian value is the value of $u$ plus one. If the
increment has no result, then the value of $u$ plus one equals $2^{|u|}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Increment of a width-constrained binary word]
\lean{Complexity.enumInc_word}
\label{Complexity.enumInc_word}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumInc, Complexity.enumInc_spec, Complexity.enumValue_injective, Complexity.enumValue_lt, Complexity.enumWord, Complexity.enumWord_length, Complexity.enumWord_value}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w$ and $i$ be natural numbers with $i<2^w$. The fixed-width increment of the
width-$w$ little-endian binary word representing $i$ is the width-$w$ word representing
$i+1$ if $i+1<2^w$, and has no result otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-Width Words and Bounded Ranks]
\lean{Complexity.enumCandidates_iff}
\label{Complexity.enumCandidates_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumValue, Complexity.enumValue_lt, Complexity.enumWord, Complexity.enumWord_complete, Complexity.enumWord_length}
\difficulty{3}
For every $w\in\mathbb{N}$ and every predicate $p$ on binary words, there exists a word
$u$ of length $w$ satisfying $p$ if and only if there exists $i\in\mathbb{N}$ with
$i<2^w$ such that the width-$w$ little-endian binary word of $i$ satisfies $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Boolean test of consecutive ranks]
\lean{Complexity.enumAny}
\label{Complexity.enumAny}
\leanok
Given an acceptance function on natural-number ranks, a start rank $i$, and a
count: the Boolean that is true exactly when one of the $\mathrm{count}$
consecutive ranks starting at $i$ accepts, evaluated by testing the ranks in
order.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Characterization of a Consecutive Rank Test]
\lean{Complexity.enumAny_iff}
\label{Complexity.enumAny_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumAny}
\difficulty{4}
Given any Boolean acceptance function $a$ on $\mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $i$ and
$\mathrm{count}$, the test of the $\mathrm{count}$ consecutive ranks starting at $i$
returns true if and only if there is a rank $j$ with $i\le j<i+\mathrm{count}$ and
$a(j)=\mathrm{true}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Certificates Among Enumerated Ranks]
\lean{Complexity.enumAny_certificates}
\label{Complexity.enumAny_certificates}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumAny, Complexity.enumAny_iff, Complexity.enumCandidates_iff, Complexity.enumWord, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{2}
Let $V\subseteq\{0,1\}^*$ be a language, and let $x$ be a binary word and
$w\in\mathbb{N}$. Testing the $2^w$ consecutive ranks starting at zero, accepting rank
$i$ exactly when $x$ concatenated with the width-$w$ little-endian binary word of $i$
belongs to $V$, returns true if and only if there is a binary word $u$ of length $w$
such that $x$ concatenated with $u$ belongs to $V$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Timed loop invariant for candidate rounds]
\lean{Complexity.enumLoop_run}
\label{Complexity.enumLoop_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumAny, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let
$\mathrm{cfg}$ assign a configuration of $M$ on $x$ to each natural-number rank. Let
$\mathrm{accept}$ be a Boolean-valued function on ranks, and let $B,i,\mathrm{count}$ be
natural numbers. Suppose the configuration at rank $i+\mathrm{count}$ is halted with
output the one-symbol word $[\mathrm{false}]$. Suppose also that for every $j$ with
$i\le j<i+\mathrm{count}$ there is a time $t\le B$ such that, if $\mathrm{accept}(j)$ is
true, the machine from $\mathrm{cfg}(j)$ is halted after $t$ steps with output
$[\mathrm{true}]$, and otherwise it reaches $\mathrm{cfg}(j+1)$ after $t$ steps. Then
there is a time $t\le \mathrm{count}\,B$ at which the machine from $\mathrm{cfg}(i)$ is
halted with output the one-symbol word containing the Boolean that is true exactly when
at least one of the $\mathrm{count}$ ranks starting at $i$ is accepted.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential bound for polynomial exponents]
\lean{Complexity.enumExponent_bound}
\label{Complexity.enumExponent_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For all natural numbers $K$ and $k$, there exist natural numbers $A$ and $e$ such that,
for every natural number $n$, $2^{K(n+1)^k}\le A(2^n)^e$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential Bound for Enumeration Budgets]
\lean{Complexity.enumBudget_bound}
\label{Complexity.enumBudget_bound}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumExponent_bound}
\difficulty{5}
For all $a,C,c,d\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist $A,e\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every
$n\in\mathbb{N}$,
\[a\cdot 2^{C(n+1)^c}\cdot\bigl(n+C(n+1)^c+1\bigr)^d\le A\cdot 2^{n^e}.\]
\end{lemma}

\label{Complexity.enumCont_inc_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumInc, Turing.incFixed}

For every Boolean word $s$, the recursively defined fixed-width little-endian increment
of $s$ agrees with the certificate-enumeration increment of $s$, including their

\begin{lemma}[Length after stalled increment]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_step_length}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_step_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_inc_eq, Complexity.enumInc, Complexity.enumInc_spec, Turing.incFixed}
\difficulty{2}
For every finite Boolean word $s$, the word obtained by applying the fixed-width
increment to $s$ and using $s$ itself if the increment overflows has length $|s|$.

\begin{lemma}[Orbit of fixed-width binary increment]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_orbit}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_orbit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_inc_eq, Complexity.enumInc_word, Complexity.enumWord, Complexity.enumWord_zero, Turing.incFixed}
\difficulty{3}
For every width $w$ and every natural number $i<2^w$, iterating the operation that

\begin{lemma}[Binary digits of a Mersenne number]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_fuel_bits}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_fuel_bits}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $w$, the binary digit list of $2^w-1$ consists of exactly $w$

\begin{definition}[Sparse tape of a finite cell list]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_sparse}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_sparse}
\leanok
The tape function determined by a finite list of possibly blank cells: a
nonnegative position $z$ holds the $z$-th list entry (which may itself be blank),
and every position beyond the list, as well as every negative position, is blank.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Appending a Sparse Tape Cell]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_sparse_append}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_sparse_append}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_sparse}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w$ be a finite list of possibly blank Boolean cells, and let $b$ be an optional
Boolean symbol. The tape function represented by the list obtained by appending $b$ to
$w$ equals the tape function represented by $w$ with its value at position $|w|$
replaced by $b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Erasing the last sparse cell]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_sparse_erase}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_sparse_erase}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_sparse, Complexity.enumCont_sparse_append}
\difficulty{3}
Let $w$ be a finite list of possibly blank Boolean cells and let $b$ be a possibly blank
Boolean cell. Blanking cell $|w|$ of the sparse tape determined by $w$ followed by $b$
gives the sparse tape determined by $w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Encoding of head moves as tape symbols]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_moveCode}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_moveCode}
\leanok
The move code is the encoding of the three head moves as tape symbols: it sends a
left move to a false bit, staying put to the blank symbol, and a right move to a
true bit.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decoding of the inverse head move]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_unmove}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_unmove}
\leanok
The inverse-move decoding is the map from recorded move symbols to head moves,
used by the backward restoration pass, that sends a false bit to a right move, the
blank symbol to staying put, and a true bit to a left move; thus every move symbol
is decoded to the inverse of the move it encodes.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Integer displacement of the decoded inverse move]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_unmove_cast}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_unmove_cast}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_moveCode, Complexity.enumCont_unmove}
\difficulty{1}
For every head move $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$, the integer displacement of the inverse move
obtained by encoding $d$ as a tape symbol and then decoding that symbol is the negative
of the integer displacement of $d$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[History entry of one machine step]
\lean{Complexity.EnumContEntry}
\label{Complexity.EnumContEntry}
\leanok
For a machine with $k$ work tapes, a history entry for one step is a pair
consisting of the tuple of the $k$ symbols under the work heads before the step
and the tuple of the $k$ head moves performed by the step.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Logging instrumentation of one action]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_logAction}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_logAction}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_moveCode, Turing.Action, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
Given the symbols currently under the $k$ work heads and an action of a $k$-tape
machine, the corresponding action of a machine with $k + (1 + (k + k))$ work
tapes: it performs the original action on the first $k$ tapes while advancing a
unary clock tape and recording, on $2k$ history tapes, the overwritten symbols and
the encoded head moves. Output and control are otherwise unchanged.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The logging machine]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_logTM}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_logTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_logAction, Turing.FinTM}
For a finite machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes, the logging machine of $M$ is the
machine with the same finite state set and initial state and with
$k + (1 + (k + k))$ work tapes, every transition of which performs $M$'s
transition on the first $k$ tapes while logging a clock mark, the overwritten
symbols, and the head moves on the extra tapes.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Logged configuration]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_logCfg}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_logCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EnumContEntry, Complexity.enumCont_moveCode, Complexity.enumCont_sparse, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
The configuration of the logging machine corresponding to a source configuration
$c$ and a finite history list $h$: the source fields occupy the first block of
tapes, the clock tape holds $|h|$ true marks, the history tapes hold the recorded
old symbols and encoded moves as sparse tapes, and every history head sits one
cell past the recorded entries.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Appending a logged step to the history]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_log_apply}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_log_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EnumContEntry, Complexity.enumCont_logAction, Complexity.enumCont_logCfg, Complexity.enumCont_sparse_append, Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
\difficulty{4}
Let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-work-tape Boolean machine on input $x$, let $h$ be a
finite list of history entries, and let $a$ be an action for that machine. Applying the
corresponding logged action to the configuration encoding $c$ and $h$ gives the encoding
of the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $c$, with the history extended by one
entry consisting of the symbols scanned before the step and the work-head movements
prescribed by $a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[History of a run]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_history}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_history}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EnumContEntry, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
For a machine, a start configuration, and a time $t$: the list of history entries
(overwritten symbols and head moves) of the actions actually executed during the
first $t$ steps of the run. No entry is recorded once the machine has halted.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Lockstep simulation with a complete history]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_log_run}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_log_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_history, Complexity.enumCont_logAction, Complexity.enumCont_logCfg, Complexity.enumCont_logTM, Complexity.enumCont_log_apply, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be an input word,
let $c_0$ be any configuration of $M$ on $x$, and let $t$ be a natural number. After $t$

\begin{definition}[The restoration machine]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_undoTM}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_undoTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_unmove, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
The restoration controller on $k + (1 + (k + k))$ work tapes: reading the newest
history entry, it alternates moving the $k$ source heads by the inverses of the
recorded moves with writing back the recorded old symbols, erasing the history as
it goes, and halts with all history heads at zero when the left blank of the
clock tape is reached. The native input head never moves.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Restoration checkpoint configuration]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_undoCfg}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_undoCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EnumContEntry, Complexity.enumCont_logCfg, Complexity.enumCont_undoTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
The checkpoint configuration of the restoration machine determined by a source
configuration $c$, a history list $h$, and an input-head position: the source
work fields are those of $c$, the logged history tapes hold $h$, and every
history head inspects the last remaining entry.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Completed restoration configuration]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_undoResult}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_undoResult}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_logCfg, Complexity.enumCont_undoTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
For a source configuration $c$ and an input-head position $p$, the completed
restoration configuration is the halted configuration of the restoration machine
whose input head is at $p$, whose source work tapes and head positions are those
of $c$, whose clock and history tapes are all blank with heads at zero, and whose
output is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Restoring a Work Tape Cell]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_restore_cell}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_restore_cell}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Action.apply_workTapes, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols}

Let $c$ be a configuration of a machine with $k$ work tapes over Boolean symbols, let
$a$ be a one-step action, and let $i$ be a work-tape index. After applying $a$ to $c$,
overwrite tape $i$ at the original head position with the symbol (or blank) that was
under that head in $c$. The resulting tape function is exactly the tape $i$ function in

\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Erasing the newest clock mark]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_clock_erase}

\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append}

\begin{definition}[Mid-restoration configuration]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_undoMid}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_undoMid}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EnumContEntry, Complexity.enumCont_logCfg, Complexity.enumCont_undoTM, Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
The intermediate restoration configuration between inverse movement and inverse
writing, for a source configuration $c$, an action $a$, and a history $h$: the

\lean{Complexity.enumCont_undo_back}

be a configuration of a $k$-work-tape machine on input $x$. For any one-step action $a$,
history list $h$, and input-head position $p$, one step of the restoration machine from
the mid-restoration configuration determined by $c,a,h,p$ is exactly the restoration
checkpoint configuration determined by $c,h,p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Restoration step on empty history]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_undo_empty}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_undo_empty}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_logCfg, Complexity.enumCont_undoCfg, Complexity.enumCont_undoResult, Complexity.enumCont_undoTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a state type, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input,
let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-work-tape machine on input $x$, and let $p$ be a
valid input-head position among the $|x|+2$ positions. Starting the restoration machine
at the checkpoint for $c$ with empty history, one step gives the completed restoration
configuration for $c$ and $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reversal of a live machine run]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_undo_run}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_undo_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_history, Complexity.enumCont_undoCfg, Complexity.enumCont_undoResult, Complexity.enumCont_undoTM, Complexity.enumCont_undo_back, Complexity.enumCont_undo_empty, Complexity.enumCont_undo_write, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean work-tape symbols, let $x$ be a finite
Boolean input, let $c_0$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$, let $p$ be a valid
input-head position among the $|x|+2$ positions, and let $t$ be a natural number.
Suppose the configuration reached by $M$ after each time $j<t$ from $c_0$ is not halted.
Then the restoration machine, started at the checkpoint for the configuration reached
after $t$ steps with the history of those $t$ steps and input-head position $p$, reaches
the completed restoration configuration for $c_0$ and $p$ after exactly $2t+1$ steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First halting time]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_first_halt}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_first_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a machine on Boolean inputs, let $c_0$ be a configuration, and let $T$ be a
natural number. If the run from $c_0$ is halted at time $T$, then there is a time $t\le
T$ such that it is not halted at any earlier time and its configuration at time $t$
equals its configuration at time $T$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Two-head administrative action]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_bufferAction}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_bufferAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
Given displacements $m$ and $d$ and a next control state, the two-head
administrative action is the action on $L + 1$ work tapes that writes nothing,
emits nothing, moves the native input head by $m$ and the head of the last
(capture) tape by $d$, leaves the heads of the first $L$ work tapes in place, and
selects the given next control state.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Entry action into restoration]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_undoEntry}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_undoEntry}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_undoTM, Turing.Action, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
The restoration entry action is the silent action that moves every history head
of the restoration machine, including the clock head, one cell left, from the right
blank onto the newest recorded entry; it writes nothing, leaves the source heads
and the input head fixed, and selects the restoration machine's checkpoint state.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Clean-call wrapper of a machine]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_cleanTM}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_cleanTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_bufferAction, Complexity.enumCont_logTM, Complexity.enumCont_undoEntry, Complexity.enumCont_undoTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.captureAction}
The clean subroutine built from a finite machine $M$: it simulates the logging
version of $M$ with the output captured on one extra final tape, then runs the
captured restoration of all source work, rewinds the native input head and the
captured word, and halts silently. The retained output word lives on the last
work tape; no physical output is emitted.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Administrative configuration of the clean wrapper]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_cleanCfg}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_cleanCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_cleanTM, Complexity.enumCont_logCfg, Complexity.enumCont_logTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
An administrative configuration of the clean-call wrapper: the source block holds
the restored work fields of a given source configuration with blank histories,
the last tape holds a retained word $y$, and the control state, native input-head
position, and capture-head position are parameters. The output is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Captured simulation phase]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_clean_capture}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_clean_capture}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_cleanTM, Complexity.enumCont_history, Complexity.enumCont_logCfg, Complexity.enumCont_logTM, Complexity.enumCont_log_run, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.captureCfg, Turing.capture_run}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $c_0$
be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$, and let $t$ be a natural number. Suppose that
$M$ is not halted at any time $j<t$ when run from $c_0$. Then the clean wrapper, run for
$t$ steps from the captured logged version of $c_0$ with empty captured prefix and
output, is in the captured logged configuration corresponding to the time-$t$
configuration of $M$ and the history of its first $t$ steps, with empty captured prefix
and output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Dispatch into captured restoration]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_clean_undo_entry}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_clean_undo_entry}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EnumContEntry, Complexity.enumCont_cleanTM, Complexity.enumCont_logCfg, Complexity.enumCont_logTM, Complexity.enumCont_undoCfg, Complexity.enumCont_undoEntry, Complexity.enumCont_undoTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.captureAction, Turing.captureCfg, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $c$ be a configuration on input $x$, and
let $h$ be a finite history list. If $c$ is halted, then one step of the clean wrapper
from the captured logged configuration of $c$ with history $h$ equals the captured
restoration checkpoint for $c$ and $h$, with $c$'s output retained on the capture tape
and empty physical output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Captured restoration bound]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_clean_restore}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_clean_restore}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_cleanCfg, Complexity.enumCont_cleanTM, Complexity.enumCont_first_halt, Complexity.enumCont_history, Complexity.enumCont_logCfg, Complexity.enumCont_logTM, Complexity.enumCont_undoCfg, Complexity.enumCont_undoResult, Complexity.enumCont_undoTM, Complexity.enumCont_undo_run, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.captureCfg, Turing.capture_run}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $c_0$ be a configuration on input $x$,
let $p$ be an input-head position, and let $t$ be a natural number. Suppose the machine
is not halted at any time $j<t$ when started from $c_0$. Then there is a time $r \le
2t+1$ at which the clean wrapper, started in its captured restoration checkpoint for the
time-$t$ configuration and its recorded history, reaches the administrative
configuration whose source work fields are restored to those of $c_0$, whose retained
word is the output after $t$ steps, whose control is in restoration phase, whose input
head is at $p$, whose capture head is at the length of that output, and whose output is
empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Administrative buffer action]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_buffer_apply}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_buffer_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_bufferAction, Complexity.enumCont_cleanCfg, Complexity.enumCont_cleanTM, Complexity.enumCont_logTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.moveInputPos}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, let $c_0$ be a
configuration of $M$ on input $x$, let $q,q'$ be optional states of the clean wrapper of
$M$, let $p$ be an input-head position, and let $h$ be an integer. For any input-head
displacement $m$ and capture-head displacement $d$, applying the buffer action with
successor state $q'$ to the administrative configuration formed from $c_0,y,q,p,h$ gives
the corresponding configuration with state $q'$, input-head position moved from $p$ by
$m$ (with boundary clamping), and capture-head position $h+d$, with its other fields
unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded Input Rewind]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_rewind}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_rewind}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val, Turing.FinTM.rewind_scan, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes over Boolean symbols, with states
$q_s,q_c$, and a possible destination state $d$ (which may be absent). Suppose every
transition from $q_s$ moves the input head left and enters $q_c$, without changing work
tapes or output. Suppose every transition from $q_c$ moves left and remains in $q_c$
when it reads a Boolean symbol, and moves right and enters $d$ when it reads a blank;
these transitions also leave work tapes and output unchanged. From any configuration $c$
whose state is $q_s$, there is a time $r\le p+2$, where $p$ is the current input-head
position, such that after $r$ steps the configuration agrees with $c$ in every field
except that its state is $d$ and its input head is at position one.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Rewinding the retained word]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_clean_buffer_rewind}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_clean_buffer_rewind}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_buffer_apply, Complexity.enumCont_cleanCfg, Complexity.enumCont_cleanTM, Complexity.enumCont_logTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, let $c_0$ be a
configuration of $M$ on input $x$, and let $p$ be an input-head position. For every
integer $j$ with $0\le j\le |y|$, the clean wrapper started in the administrative
configuration with retained word $y$, control state $4$, input-head position $p$, and
capture-head position $j-1$ reaches after exactly $j+1$ steps the administrative
configuration with the same retained word and input-head position, control state $5$,
and capture-head position zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clean completion of a halting computation]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_clean_complete}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_clean_complete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_bufferAction, Complexity.enumCont_buffer_apply, Complexity.enumCont_cleanCfg, Complexity.enumCont_cleanTM, Complexity.enumCont_clean_buffer_rewind, Complexity.enumCont_clean_capture, Complexity.enumCont_clean_restore, Complexity.enumCont_clean_undo_entry, Complexity.enumCont_first_halt, Complexity.enumCont_history, Complexity.enumCont_logCfg, Complexity.enumCont_rewind, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.captureCfg, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $c_0$ be a configuration on input $x$,
and let $y$ be a Boolean word. If after $T$ steps from $c_0$ the machine is halted and
its output is $y$, then there is a time $\tau \le 3T+|x|+|y|+8$ at which the clean
wrapper, started from the captured logged configuration of $c_0$ with empty captured
word and output, reaches the administrative configuration with the source work fields
restored to those of $c_0$, the retained word $y$, halted control, input head at
position $1$, capture head at position $0$, and empty output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[The assembly machine]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_concatTM}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_concatTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
A two-state machine with one work tape that first emits (copies to its output)
the entire native input and then emits the word written on its work tape, never
writing that tape, and halts at the word's right blank.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Assembly configurations]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_concatCfg}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_concatCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
An assembly configuration is the configuration of the assembly machine on input
$x$ determined by a control state, an input-head position, a candidate word $s$
held fixed on the single work tape with its head at a given cell, and the output
prefix emitted so far.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Input phase of assembly]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_concat_native}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_concat_native}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_concatCfg, Complexity.enumCont_concatTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.FinTM.inputSymbol_at, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$, $s$, $\mathit{pre}$, and $\mathit{rest}$ be Boolean words, and suppose
$x=\mathit{pre}\mathbin{+\!\!+}\mathit{rest}$. After exactly $|\mathit{rest}|+1$ steps
from the assembly configuration in input phase, with input head at position
$|\mathit{pre}|+1$, candidate tape containing $s$ with its head at position $0$, and
output $\mathit{pre}$, the machine is in candidate phase with input head at the right
boundary, candidate tape and head unchanged, and output $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Candidate phase of assembly]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_concat_candidate}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_concat_candidate}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_concatCfg, Complexity.enumCont_concatTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$, $s$, $\mathit{pre}$, and $\mathit{rest}$ be Boolean words, let $p$ be an
input-head position for input $x$, and let $\mathit{out}$ be a Boolean word. If
$s=\mathit{pre}\mathbin{+\!\!+}\mathit{rest}$, then after exactly $|\mathit{rest}|+1$
steps from the assembly configuration in candidate phase, with input head at $p$,
candidate tape containing $s$ with its head at position $|\mathit{pre}|$, and output
$\mathit{out}\mathbin{+\!\!+}\mathit{pre}$, the machine is halted with the candidate tape
unchanged, its head at position $|s|$, input head still at $p$, and output
$\mathit{out}\mathbin{+\!\!+}s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Concatenation machine run]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_concat_run}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_concat_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_concatCfg, Complexity.enumCont_concatTM, Complexity.enumCont_concat_candidate, Complexity.enumCont_concat_native, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{3}
For any Boolean words $x$ and $s$, running the assembly machine on input $x$ from its
initial configuration with $s$ on its work tape for $|x|+|s|+2$ steps gives a halted
configuration. Its input head is at the right boundary blank, its work tape stores $s$
with the head at position $|s|$, and its output is $x$ followed by $s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Buffered Sequential Composition Bound]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_prepared_comp}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_prepared_comp}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_first_halt, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg_rewind, Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg_run, Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg_run, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite deterministic machines over Boolean symbols, and let $c_0$
be any configuration of $M_1$ on input $x$. Suppose that after $T_1$ steps from $c_0$,
$M_1$ is halted and its output is the word $y$, and that $M_2$ computes output $z$ from
input $y$ in time $T_2$. Then there is a time $t\le T_1+|y|+2+T_2$ at which the buffered
sequential composition, started from the first-phase configuration associated with
$c_0$, is halted and has output $z$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Canonical Candidate Seam]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_round_seam}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_round_seam}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_concatTM, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M_V$ be a finite machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$ and $s$ be Boolean words,
and let $b$ be a Boolean phase. The buffered composition of the assembly machine with
$M_V$, started from the assembly machine's configuration on input $x$ with phase $b$ and
word $s$ on its work tape, equals the configuration on input $x$ whose state is the
first-phase state corresponding to $b$, whose tape zero stores $s$, whose other work
tapes are blank with heads at zero, whose input head is at position one, and whose
output is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Time bound for a prepared verifier call]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_verifier_call}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_verifier_call}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_concatTM, Complexity.enumCont_concat_run, Complexity.enumCont_prepared_comp, Complexity.enumCont_round_seam, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M_V$ be a finite Turing machine deciding a language $V$ over Boolean words within
time $T_V$, and let $x,s$ be Boolean words. From the canonical seam configuration with
$s$ on the designated work tape and input $x$, the buffered composition of the assembly
machine with $M_V$ reaches, in some $t\le T_V(|x|+|s|)+2(|x|+|s|)+4$ steps, a halted
configuration whose output is the one-symbol word containing the indicator of $x$
concatenated with $s$ belonging to $V$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Halt-redirecting action wrapper]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_returnAction}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_returnAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
Relabel the live states of an action along an embedding and redirect its halt to
a designated live return state, keeping all tape effects and the output
unchanged.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Halt-redirecting configuration map]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_returnCfg}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_returnCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
The configuration correspondence matching the halt redirection: all fields are
preserved, and the control state is the embedded live state, or the designated
return state when the source has halted.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Simulation Through Halt Redirection]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_return_run}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_return_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_returnAction, Complexity.enumCont_returnCfg, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ and $H$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over Boolean symbols, let
$e$ map states of $M$ into states of $H$, and choose a return state $r$ of $H$. Suppose
that, on every state, input reading, and work-tape reading, the transition of $H$ from
the embedded state is the action of $M$ with its successor state embedded when present
and redirected to $r$ when absent, leaving all other action components unchanged. If $M$
is live at every time $j<t$ when run from a configuration $c_0$ on input $x$, then the
run of $H$ for $t$ steps from the configuration obtained by embedding the state of $c_0$
(or using $r$ if it is halted) and preserving its other fields equals the configuration
obtained by applying the same state correspondence to the time-$t$ configuration of $M$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Padding an action to a larger tape bank]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_padAction}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_padAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
Given a map $\iota$ from source control states to host control states, the padding
of an action $a$ of a $k$-tape machine to $K$ tapes is the action that performs
$a$'s input move, output, writes and moves on the first $k$ work tapes, leaves
every further tape unwritten and stationary, and replaces $a$'s next control state
by its image under $\iota$ (halting stays halting).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Padding a configuration to a larger tape bank]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_padCfg}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_padCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
Pad a configuration of a $k$-tape machine to $K$ tapes by adding blank stationary
high tapes, embedding the control state along a given map.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Padding commutes with applying an action]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_pad_apply}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_pad_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_padAction, Complexity.enumCont_padCfg, Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k,K$ be natural numbers, let $S,H$ be types, let $	ext{emb}:S\to H$ be a map, let
$x$ be a Boolean input word, let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-tape machine with
states in $S$, and let $a$ be an action of that machine. Applying the action padded
along $	ext{emb}$ to the padded configuration equals padding along $	ext{emb}$ of the
configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Simulation on a padded tape bank]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_pad_run}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_pad_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_padAction, Complexity.enumCont_padCfg, Complexity.enumCont_pad_apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_comm_of_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k\le K$, let $S,H$ be types, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $M$ be a $k$-tape
machine with states in $S$, let $N$ be a $K$-tape machine with states in $H$, and let
$	ext{emb}:S\to H$. Suppose that for every source state, input symbol, and $K$-tuple of
scanned work-tape symbols, $N$'s transition at the embedded state equals the padded
action obtained from $M$'s transition using the first $k$ scanned symbols. Then for
every source configuration $c$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, running $N$ for $t$ steps
from the padded configuration of $c$ gives the padding of the configuration reached by
running $M$ from $c$ for $t$ steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Three source routines on a shared tape bank]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_sources}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_sources}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_padAction, Turing.FinTM}
The disjoint union of three finite machines on a common bank whose size is the
sum of their tape counts: each branch runs its machine, padded, on an initial
block of tapes. The machine starts in the third routine, and control can enter
either other routine without disturbing tape zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Two-ended candidate/capture action]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_endsAction}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_endsAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
Given optional writes $a$ and $b$, a displacement $d$, and a next control state,
the two-ended action is the action on $L + 1$ work tapes that performs write $a$ on
tape zero and write $b$ on the last tape, moves both of these heads by $d$, leaves
every intervening tape unwritten and stationary, keeps the input head fixed, and
emits nothing.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The enumerator body]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_bodyTM}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_bodyTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_cleanTM, Complexity.enumCont_endsAction, Complexity.enumCont_logTM, Complexity.enumCont_returnAction, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
Let $B$ be a finite source machine with designated verification and increment
entry states. The enumerator body built from $B$ is the machine that issues clean
calls of $B$ (with halts redirected to live administrative states) for
initialization, verification, and increment, coordinated by seven administrative
states: an anchor, a seed-copy phase, an unused reserve, a verdict test, an
increment check, a result copy, and a synchronized rewind. Its stopped variant
agrees with the active body except that the anchor is a silent self-loop.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Time bound for an increment call]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_increment_call}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_increment_call}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_concatCfg, Complexity.enumCont_concatTM, Complexity.enumCont_concat_candidate, Complexity.enumCont_prepared_comp, Complexity.enumCont_round_seam, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.incFixed, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine and let $j$ be a natural number.
Suppose that on every Boolean input $u$, machine $I$ halts within $j(|u|+1)$ steps and
outputs the fixed-width increment of $u$, using the empty word when that increment
overflows. Then for any Boolean words $x$ and $s$, there is a time $t\le (j+3)(|s|+1)$
at which the buffered composition of the assembly machine with $I$, started in its
candidate phase with $s$ on its first work tape and input $x$, is halted and has output
equal to the fixed-width increment of $s$, with overflow represented by the empty word.
\end{lemma}

$	ext{emb}:S\to H$ be a map, let $q:S$, and let $x,s$ be Boolean words. Padding the seam
configuration on input $x$ with state $q$, word $s$ on tape zero, and empty words on all
other tapes of the $k$-tape bank gives the seam configuration on the $K$-tape bank with
state $	ext{emb}(q)$, word $s$ on tape zero, and empty words on all other tapes.
\end{lemma}

\lean{Complexity.enumCont_pad_init}

$q:S$, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. Padding the initial configuration with state
$q$ on input $x$ gives the seam configuration on the $K$-tape bank with state

\end{lemma}

tape store their concatenation. Replacing the tape content at the integer cell
$|\mathrm{pre}|$ by $b$ gives the buffer tape storing $\mathrm{pre}$ followed by $b$ and
then by $\mathrm{old}$ with its first symbol dropped.
\end{lemma}

Blanking cell $p$ of the sparse tape determined by $p$ blank entries followed by the
entries $b$ and $r$ gives the sparse tape determined by $p+1$ blank entries followed by

\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Two-ended administrative configurations]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_pairCfg}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_pairCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
A configuration on $L + 1$ work tapes for the administrative copy and rewind
scans: tape zero and the last tape carry given tape functions with a common head
position, every other tape is blank with its head at zero, the input head is at
cell one, and the output is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Effect of a two-ended action]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_ends_apply}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_ends_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_endsAction, Complexity.enumCont_pairCfg, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $L>0$, let $q,q'$ be optional states, let $u,v$ be tape contents indexed by the
integers, let $h$ be an integer head position, and let $a,b$ be optional writes and
$d\in\{-1,0,1\}$ a displacement. Applying the two-ended action to the configuration with
tape contents $u,v$ at the two ends, all intermediate tapes blank, and both end heads at
$h$ gives the corresponding configuration in state $q'$, with the end cells at $h$
changed according to the writes and the heads at $h+d$. An absent write leaves that cell
unchanged; a present write may place either a Boolean symbol or a blank, while the
input-head position and empty output remain as in the two-ended configuration.
\end{lemma}

is the everywhere-blank tape.

\begin{lemma}[Copy scan of a captured suffix]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_copy_scan}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_copy_scan}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_endsAction, Complexity.enumCont_ends_apply, Complexity.enumCont_overwrite, Complexity.enumCont_pairCfg, Complexity.enumCont_sparse, Complexity.enumCont_sparse_blanks, Complexity.enumCont_sparse_clear, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{5}
Let $L>0$, let a machine have $L+1$ work tapes, let $q_c,q_r$ be states, and let $f$ be
a Boolean map. Suppose that in state $q_c$ the machine reads the last tape: on a symbol
$b$ it writes $f(b)$ on tape zero, blanks the last tape, moves both heads right, and
remains in $q_c$; on a blank it makes no writes, moves both heads left, and enters
$q_r$. For Boolean words $\mathit{pre},\mathit{old},\mathit{rest}$, start with the heads
at position $|\mathit{pre}|$, tape zero storing $\mathit{pre}$ followed by
$\mathit{old}$, and the last tape storing $\mathit{rest}$ starting at position
$|\mathit{pre}|$ with all earlier cells blank. After $|\mathit{rest}|+1$ steps the
machine is in state $q_r$, the last tape is blank, tape zero stores $\mathit{pre}$
followed by the image of $\mathit{rest}$ under $f$ and then the suffix of $\mathit{old}$
after its first $|\mathit{rest}|$ symbols, and both heads are at position
$|\mathit{pre}|+|\mathit{rest}|-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Synchronized Rewind of Endpoint Heads]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_pair_rewind}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_pair_rewind}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_endsAction, Complexity.enumCont_ends_apply, Complexity.enumCont_pairCfg, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{5}
Let $L>0$, let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $L+1$ work tapes and Boolean symbols,
and let $q_r,q_a$ be states. Suppose that in state $q_r$, on every input and work-tape
reading, the machine moves both endpoint heads one cell left and enters $q_r$ if tape
zero is nonblank, and moves both one cell right and enters $q_a$ if tape zero is blank;
it makes no writes or output. For every Boolean word $w$ and every $j\le |w|$, starting
with both endpoint heads at $j-1$, tape zero storing $w$, the last tape blank, and state
$q_r$, after exactly $j+1$ steps the configuration has state $q_a$, both endpoint heads
at zero, tape zero still storing $w$, and the last tape blank; all other configuration
fields agree with the prescribed initial and final two-ended configurations.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Complete copy and rewind]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_copy_complete}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_copy_complete}

\difficulty{3}

a Boolean map. Suppose that in state $q_c$ the machine reads the last tape: on a symbol
$b$ it writes $f(b)$ on tape zero, blanks the last tape, moves both heads right, and
remains in $q_c$; on a blank it makes no writes, moves both heads left, and enters
$q_r$. Suppose that in state $q_r$ it reads tape zero: on a symbol it makes no writes,
moves both heads left, and remains in $q_r$; on a blank it makes no writes, moves both
heads right, and enters $q_a$. For words $\mathit{old}$ and $v$ with $|\mathit{old}|\le
|v|$, starting with the two heads at zero, tape zero storing $\mathit{old}$, and the
last tape storing $v$, after $2|v|+2$ steps the machine is in state $q_a$, tape zero
stores the word obtained by applying $f$ to each symbol of $v$, the last tape is blank,
and both heads are at zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Absorption by a silent self-loop]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_absorb}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_absorb}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, let
$q_a$ be a state, and suppose that in state $q_a$ the transition is always the action
that keeps the input head fixed, makes no changes or movements on the work tapes, emits
no output, and returns to $q_a$. Then, from any configuration on any Boolean input whose
state is $q_a$, iterating the machine's step function any finite number of times leaves
the entire configuration unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Agreement of runs before an anchor visit]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_agree_run}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_agree_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ and $N$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet
and state set $S$, and designate a state $q_a$. Suppose their transitions agree in every
state other than $q_a$, for every input symbol and every tuple of work-tape readings.
For any configuration $c$ on input $x$ and any $t\in\mathbb N$, if the run of $N$ from
$c$ is never in state $q_a$ at any time $j<t$, then the two machines' configurations
after $t$ steps from $c$ are equal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First visit to an anchor state]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_first_anchor}

\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ and $M_0$ be machines with the same number of work tapes and state set, and let
$q_a$ be a state. Suppose their transition rules agree at every state other than $q_a$,
and that $M_0$ at $q_a$ makes a stationary, silent transition back to $q_a$. For a
configuration $c$ and time $T$, if the run of $M_0$ from $c$ is in state $q_a$ at time
$T$, then some $t\le T$ has the property that the run of $M$ is never in state $q_a$ at
any earlier time and its configuration at time $t$ equals the configuration of $M_0$ at
time $T$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Transfer of halted runs]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_halt_transfer}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_halt_transfer}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a state set, let $x$ be a Boolean input word,
and let $M$ and $N$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes and Boolean symbols,
with $q_a\in S$. Suppose their transition actions agree in every state other than $q_a$,
and in state $q_a$ machine $N$ takes the control action that stays on the input head and
returns to $q_a$ without writing, moving work heads, or emitting output. If the run of
$N$ from a configuration $c$ is halted after $T$ steps, then the run of $M$ from $c$ has
the same configuration after $T$ steps, and at every time $j\le T$ its state is not
$q_a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Guarded body initialization]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_body_start_guarded}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_body_start_guarded}
\leanok

states of $B$, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. Suppose that, from its initial
configuration on $x$, with all work tapes blank, $B$ halts at time $T$ and outputs $w$
consecutive true bits. Then for some $t\le 3T+|x|+3w+10$, the body machine with
parameters $B,q_v,q_i$ and stopped flag false, started in its initial configuration on
$x$, reaches the anchor on the seam carrying $w$ false bits on tape zero and blank
contents on all other tapes; at every time $j<t$, its state is not the anchor state.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Guarded body round]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_body_round_guarded}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_body_round_guarded}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_bodyTM, Complexity.enumCont_body_agree, Complexity.enumCont_body_depart, Complexity.enumCont_body_round_raw, Complexity.enumCont_first_anchor, Complexity.enumCont_halt_transfer, Complexity.enumCont_pairCfg, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.incFixed, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{5}
Let $B$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine with at least one work tape, let $q_v,q_i$ be
states of $B$, and let $x,s$ be Boolean words. Suppose that from the seam configuration
on input $x$ with state $q_v$ and word assignment placing $s$ on tape zero, $B$ halts
within $T_v$ steps with output $[b]$, and from the corresponding configuration with
state $q_i$, it halts within $T_i$ steps with output equal to the fixed-width increment
of $s$, using the empty word if that increment overflows. Then there is an integer $t$
with $0<t\le 3T_v+3T_i+2|x|+3|s|+22$ such that, in the body machine with stopped flag
false started at its anchor on the seam carrying $s$, no strictly intermediate
positive-time configuration is at the anchor; at time $t$, if $b$ is true the machine is
halted with output $[\mathrm{true}]$, and if $b$ is false it is at the anchor on the
seam carrying the increment of $s$, with $s$ itself used when the increment overflows.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{2}
Let $M$ and $B$ be finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machines with $M$ using a positive
number of work tapes and no more work tapes than $B$. Let $e$ map the states of $M$ to
states of $B$, and suppose that for every source state and every input/work-tape scan,
$B$'s transition at the embedded state is the padded action of $M$'s transition, reading
$M$'s work tapes from the corresponding initial block. If $M$, started in state $q$ on
input $x$ with word $s$ on its first work tape and all remaining tapes blank, is halted
at time $T$ with output $y$, then $B$, started in state $e(q)$ on input $x$ with the
same initial tape contents, is halted at time $T$ with output $y$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lifting an initial computation]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_lift_init}

\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ and $B$ be finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machines, with $M$ using no more work
tapes than $B$. Let $e$ map the states of $M$ to states of $B$, and suppose that at
every embedded state and for every input/work-tape scan, $B$ takes the padded action of
$M$, reading the corresponding initial work-tape block. If $M$ computes output $y$ from
input $x$ in time $T$, then $B$, started in state $e(q_0)$ with all work tapes blank on
input $x$, is halted at time $T$ and has output $y$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Enumerator from body contracts]
\lean{Complexity.enumCont_from_body}
\label{Complexity.enumCont_from_body}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_fuel_bits, Complexity.enumCont_orbit, Complexity.enumCont_step_length, Complexity.enumWord, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_polyUnary, Turing.FinTM.exists_loopCfgTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.incFixed, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{6}
Let $C,c$ be natural numbers, let $G$ be a natural-number-valued function, let $V$ be a
language of Boolean words, and let $B$ be a finite Boolean-input Turing machine with
designated state $q_a$. Suppose that for every Boolean input $x$, the run of $B$ from
its initial configuration reaches, at some time at most $G(|x|)$, state $q_a$ with the
all-false word of width $w=C(|x|+1)^c$ on tape zero and all other tapes blank, and has
not visited $q_a$ earlier. Suppose also that for every $x$ and every word $s$ of length
$w$, the run from state $q_a$ with $s$ on tape zero and other tapes blank reaches, in
positive time at most $G(|x|)$ and without an intervening positive-time visit to $q_a$,
either a halted configuration with output true if $x$ followed by $s$ belongs to $V$, or
the configuration at state $q_a$ with the fixed-width increment of $s$ on tape zero and
all other tapes blank if it does not. Then there are a natural number $b$ and a finite
Boolean-input Turing machine $E$ such that for every Boolean input $x$ there is a
sequence of configurations indexed by the natural numbers and a startup time at most
$b\bigl(G(|x|)+(|x|+1)^{c+1}+1\bigr)$. The run of $E$ reaches the sequence's initial
configuration at that startup time; its configuration at index $2^w$ is halted with
output false; and for every index $i<2^w$, some run time at most the same bound takes
the configuration at index $i$ either to a halted configuration with output true when
$x$ followed by the width-$w$ binary representation of $i$ belongs to $V$, or to the
configuration at index $i+1$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Enumerator configuration and time contracts]
\lean{Complexity.enumMachine_contracts}
\label{Complexity.enumMachine_contracts}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.enumCont_bodyTM, Complexity.enumCont_body_round_guarded, Complexity.enumCont_body_start_guarded, Complexity.enumCont_concatTM, Complexity.enumCont_from_body, Complexity.enumCont_increment_call, Complexity.enumCont_lift_call, Complexity.enumCont_lift_init, Complexity.enumCont_sources, Complexity.enumCont_verifier_call, Complexity.enumWord, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_incFixed, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_polyUnary, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.incFixed}
\difficulty{6}
Let $C,c$ be natural numbers, let $V$ be a language of Boolean words, let $T_V$ be a
time bound, and let $M_V$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine that decides $V$ within
time $T_V$. Then there exist a natural number $b$ and a finite Boolean Turing machine
$E$ such that for every Boolean input $x$ there are a family of configurations
$\mathrm{cfg}(i)$ of $E$ on $x$, indexed by natural numbers, and a startup time
satisfying the following conditions. Writing $w=C(|x|+1)^c$, the startup time is at most
$b\bigl(T_V(|x|+w)+(|x|+w+1)^{c+1}\bigr)$, and $E$ reaches $\mathrm{cfg}(0)$ from its
initial configuration within that startup time. The configuration $\mathrm{cfg}(2^w)$ is
halted with output $[\mathrm{false}]$. For every $i<2^w$, there is a time at most
$b\bigl(T_V(|x|+w)+(|x|+w+1)^{c+1}\bigr)$ such that, if $x$ concatenated with the
width-$w$ little-endian binary word of $i$ belongs to $V$, the machine from
$\mathrm{cfg}(i)$ halts with output $[\mathrm{true}]$; otherwise it reaches
$\mathrm{cfg}(i+1)$ at that time.
\end{theorem}

Let $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $V$ be a language of binary strings, let
$T_v:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and let $M_V$ be a finite binary Turing machine that
decides $V$ within time $T_v$. Then there are $b\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite binary
Turing machine deciding the language $\{x:\exists u,\ |u|=C(|x|+1)^c\text{ and }xu\in
V\}$ within time, on inputs of length $n$,
$b\,2^{C(n+1)^c}\bigl(T_v(n+C(n+1)^c)+(n+C(n+1)^c+1)^{c+1}\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

to the exit state, and then emits the single symbol found on tape zero as its
decision.

position $h$: its control state is phase $q$, its input head is at $p$, tape zero
holds $u$ with its head at $h$, every other work tape is blank with its head at
zero, and the output is empty.
\end{definition}

\uses{Complexity.a3RunTM, Complexity.a3_run_call, Complexity.a3_run_start, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with at least one work
tape, and let $\mathrm{entry}$ and $\mathrm{exit}$ be states of $C$. Let $x$ be a
Boolean word, $b$ a Boolean value, and $t>0$. Suppose that the run of $C$ from the
canonical entry configuration carrying $x$ on tape zero is not in state $\mathrm{exit}$
at any time $j$ with $0<j<t$, and at time $t$ reaches the canonical exit configuration
carrying the singleton word $[b]$ on tape zero. Then the wrapper computes $[b]$ from
input $x$ within $2\operatorname{length}(x)+2+t+1$ steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cleaning a binary decider]
\lean{Complexity.a3_decider_clean}

\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of
binary strings, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $M$ decides $L$ within time $T$,
then there exist a finite binary Turing machine $R$ and a natural number $B$ such that
$R$ decides $L$ within time $n\mapsto B\bigl(T(n)+n+2\bigr)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Timed buffered composition]
\lean{Complexity.a3_comp_at}
\label{Complexity.a3_comp_at}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferedComp_start, Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg_run, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{3}
Let $F,G$ be finite Turing machines over the binary alphabet, let $x,y,z$ be binary
words, and let $s,t\in\mathbb{N}$. If $F$ computes $y$ from $x$ within $s$ steps and $G$
computes $z$ from $y$ within $t$ steps, then their buffered sequential composition
computes $z$ from $x$ within $s+|y|+2+t$ steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Nonempty-input guard]
\lean{Complexity.a3NonemptyTM}
\label{Complexity.a3NonemptyTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
For a finite machine $M$, the nonempty-input guard of $M$ is the machine with the
same work tapes that, on empty input, emits a single rejecting (false) bit and
halts, and, on nonempty input, takes one silent step and then runs $M$ from $M$'s
initial state.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Run preserved under state renaming]
\lean{Complexity.a3_nonempty_run}
\label{Complexity.a3_nonempty_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3NonemptyTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_comm_of_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean input
word, and let $c$ be any configuration of $M$ on input $x$. For every natural number
$t$, running the machine that guards against empty input for $t$ steps from the
configuration obtained by renaming the states of $c$ gives the state-renamed
configuration reached by running $M$ from $c$ for $t$ steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Empty-input rejection by the guard]
\lean{Complexity.a3_nonempty_nil}
\label{Complexity.a3_nonempty_nil}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3NonemptyTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{2}
For every finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet, the nonempty-input guard
of $M$, on the empty input, halts after one step and outputs exactly the one-symbol word
$[\mathrm{false}]$, using some amount of work-tape space.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Guarded computation on nonempty input]
\lean{Complexity.a3_nonempty_computes}
\label{Complexity.a3_nonempty_computes}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3NonemptyTM, Complexity.a3_nonempty_run, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $x$ and $y$ be
Boolean words with $x$ nonempty. If $M$ computes $y$ from $x$ within $t$ steps, then the
machine that guards against empty input computes $y$ from $x$ within $t+1$ steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Strict monotonicity of exponential padding]
\lean{Complexity.a3_split_strictMono}
\label{Complexity.a3_split_strictMono}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For all natural numbers $C$ and $c$, the function on the natural numbers given by
$n\mapsto n+C\cdot 2^{(n+1)^c}$ is strictly increasing.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[The exponential-split search]
\lean{Complexity.a3Split}
\label{Complexity.a3Split}
\leanok
Given constants $C, c$ and a length $m$: the least $n \le m$ satisfying
$n + C \cdot 2^{(n+1)^c} = m$, if one exists, and an explicit failure value
otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Specification of a successful split]
\lean{Complexity.a3_split_spec}
\label{Complexity.a3_split_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3Split}
\difficulty{2}
For natural numbers $C,c,m,n$, if the exponential-split search on $(C,c,m)$ returns $n$,
then $n\le m$ and $n+C\cdot 2^{(n+1)^c}=m$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Failure of the split search]
\lean{Complexity.a3_split_none_iff}
\label{Complexity.a3_split_none_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3Split}
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $C,c,m$, the exponential-split search fails exactly when there is no
natural number $n$ satisfying $n+C\cdot 2^{(n+1)^c}=m$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Completeness of the split search]
\lean{Complexity.a3_split_complete}
\label{Complexity.a3_split_complete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3Split, Complexity.a3_split_none_iff, Complexity.a3_split_spec, Complexity.a3_split_strictMono}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C,c,m,n$ be natural numbers. If $n+C\cdot 2^{(n+1)^c}=m$, then the
exponential-split search with parameters $C,c,m$ returns $n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[No split at length zero]
\lean{Complexity.a3_split_empty}
\label{Complexity.a3_split_empty}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3Split, Complexity.a3_split_none_iff}
\difficulty{2}
Let $C$ be a positive natural number and let $c$ be a natural number. The
exponential-split search with parameters $C,c$ at length $0$ returns no value.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[The emitted split word]
\lean{Complexity.a3SplitWord}
\label{Complexity.a3SplitWord}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3Split, Turing.pairEncode}
Given constants $C, c$ and a word $y$, the split word of $y$ is the paired encoding
of the first $i$ symbols of $y$ and the remaining suffix when the exponential-split
search on $(C, c, |y|)$ returns $i$, and is the empty word, signalling failure,
when the search fails.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Length bound for the split word]
\lean{Complexity.a3_split_length}
\label{Complexity.a3_split_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3Split, Complexity.a3SplitWord, Complexity.a3_split_spec, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $C$ and $c$ and a finite Boolean word $y$, the length of the split
word of $y$ is at most $2|y|+2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial time for split-word computation]
\lean{Complexity.a3_split_timed}
\label{Complexity.a3_split_timed}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3Split, Complexity.a3SplitWord, Complexity.a3_exp_bits_timed, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_splitSolveWith, Turing.solveSplitWith}
\difficulty{5}
For every pair of natural numbers $C,c$, there exist a finite Turing machine over the
binary alphabet and a natural number $A$ such that, on every binary input of length $n$,
the machine computes the split word in exactly $A(n+1)^{c+2}$ steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[The padding verifier]
\lean{Complexity.a3Verifier}
\label{Complexity.a3Verifier}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3Split}
For a language $L$ over the binary alphabet and a degree $c$: the language of
words $y$ such that the exponential-split search with coefficient one succeeds
on $|y|$ with some prefix length $n$ and the first $n$ symbols of $y$ form a
word in $L$. Words whose length admits no split are rejected; certificate bits
carry no information.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Verifier on padded concatenations]
\lean{Complexity.a3_verifier_append}
\label{Complexity.a3_verifier_append}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3Split, Complexity.a3Verifier, Complexity.a3_split_complete}
\difficulty{2}
Let $L$ be a language of binary words, let $c$ be a natural number, and let $x,u$ be
binary words with $|u|=2^{(|x|+1)^c}$. Then $x$ followed by $u$ belongs to the padding
verifier for $L$ at degree $c$ if and only if $x\in L$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bound from the split equation]
\lean{Complexity.a3_source_budget}
\label{Complexity.a3_source_budget}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.a3Split, Complexity.a3_split_spec}
\difficulty{3}
Let $a,c,m,n$ be natural numbers. If the exponential-split search with coefficient $1$,
degree $c$, and length $m$ returns $n$, then $a\cdot 2^{n^c}\le a\cdot m$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time membership of the verifier]
\lean{Complexity.a3_verifier_mem_P}
\label{Complexity.a3_verifier_mem_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.a3NonemptyTM, Complexity.a3Split, Complexity.a3SplitWord, Complexity.a3Verifier, Complexity.a3_comp_at, Complexity.a3_decider_clean, Complexity.a3_nonempty_computes, Complexity.a3_nonempty_nil, Complexity.a3_source_budget, Complexity.a3_split_length, Complexity.a3_split_spec, Complexity.a3_split_timed, Complexity.mem_P_iff, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairFst, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $L$ be a language of binary words, and let $a,c$ be natural numbers and $M$ a finite
Turing machine over the binary alphabet. If $M$ decides $L$ within time $n\mapsto a\cdot
2^{n^c}$, then the padding verifier for $L$ at degree $c$ belongs to $\mathrm{P}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential Time Is Contained in Nondeterministic Exponential Time]
\lean{Complexity.EXP_subset_NEXP}
\label{Complexity.EXP_subset_NEXP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EXP, Complexity.NEXP, Complexity.a3Verifier, Complexity.a3_verifier_append, Complexity.a3_verifier_mem_P}
\difficulty{3}
Every language in $\mathrm{EXP}$ belongs to $\mathrm{NEXP}$, where membership in
$\mathrm{NEXP}$ means that there are natural numbers $C,c$ and a language
$V\in\mathsf{P}$ such that, for every binary string $x$, membership of $x$ is equivalent
to the existence of a string $u$ of length exactly $C\cdot 2^{(|x|+1)^c}$ for which the
concatenation $xu$ belongs to $V$.
\end{theorem}
